# Independent review: full-theta radial Gram divisor obstruction

Verdict: ACCEPT_RADIAL_GRAM_QUOTIENT_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.
Candidate: RADIAL_GRAM_DIVISOR_PREFLIGHT.md, 12311 bytes, SHA256
5ad591b682967eed85ada4f667c77dbbe624fca66a4644a905f52b5075229bce.
Source base: 8e63d0a557758bd61c307f5bfa9156194ecfea72.
Reviewer: /root/pairzero_geometry_review. Date: 2026-09-17.

Q1--Q8 are sound with their stated full-source premises. No correction is
required. The result excludes all-finite PSD of this precise quotient
V/G on any real open interval and excludes its stated PSD tensor repairs.
It neither makes original V negative nor improves a lower bound for V;
original full positivity and RH remain open.

## Direct inputs and scope of verification

The complete candidate was read and its size/hash verified. Directly
read or rechecked unchanged source inputs are:

- FULL_V_RANK_TWO_INTAKE, including complete Gram comparison R1--R8:
  51168fb802d7facfb74291d0a3fc0009b121f540711df2fe10ae01cd84c1d14f.
- LOGVCURV_INTAKE:
  074a6ee11edf58ed502f8a41454515c06b5d286605b53ff0fe9e889981a3b929.
- PAIRZERO_GEOMETRY:
  c53ae234d3ad87728203b9e64439eb718a79e0b13c09d2f18d9e9a481f31bccd.
- Full LOGVCURV raw response, 55333 bytes:
  e33ee8eee31a36c6b2de2e590f8c4ce94a658ed20662f505df204d7592e364f5.
  LV2, LV12--LV18 and the following original-integral bounds were read
  directly again, retaining both full source series and arbitrary zero
  multiplicity.
- Separate quotient lemma:
  4c36857d42473687aaf7744f69a5de51a5ab5bd38bf6ad3a292f293902586a07.
  Its independent review:
  a0757c728d2ffd5ba03b1c2b6a6f739c3a63b80e18df4641b293e9475b631f4a.

The published strict concavity and the already accepted existence of a
nonreal spatial f zero are named inputs; this review does not claim a
new proof of the published concavity theorem or reclassify those zeros
as xi zeros. No new external theorem, search, numerical source test,
descendant, Pro dispatch, or repository edit was performed. Only this
assigned staging review is written.

## Q1: exact sufficient target and its rank-two boundary

The input report gives the complete radial Gram G, equality G(x,x)=V(x,x),
and strict entry comparison 0<V(x,y)<G(x,y) for distinct real nodes.
Therefore R has diagonal one and off-diagonal entries in (0,1), making
all its two-node matrices PSD (strictly positive for distinct nodes).
All-finite R PSD would indeed imply V PSD by the Schur product theorem.
The converse is neither used nor true in general. Thus disproving this
particular sufficient condition is logically compatible with V positivity.

## Q2: branch-independent holomorphy on the entire source strip

Let z=a+ib and let u+iv be either square root of s+z^2. Squaring the
proposed upper comparison gives exactly

    (s+a^2+b^2)^2-[(s+a^2-b^2)^2+4a^2b^2]=4sb^2>=0.

Both compared square-root quantities are nonnegative. It follows that
v^2<=b^2, so every possible root remains in S. Opposite root choices give
the same f value because f is even on S. Near a zero of s+z^2, the even
Taylor series f(w)=sum a_(2k)w^(2k) becomes a convergent series in s+z^2.
This proves actual removability at the branch points and a single-valued
holomorphic g_z(s), rather than selecting an unjustified global branch.

For compact z sets the large-s root with positive real part is
sqrt(s)+O(s^(-1/2)), with imaginary part uniformly inside S. LV2 therefore
provides the claimed double-exponential envelope. Its square is integrable
in ds; bounded finite s intervals are covered by compactness and the
removable branch points. Pointwise holomorphy and this local norm bound
justify L2-valued holomorphy, for example by dominated Cauchy integrals.
The bilinear integral for G is jointly holomorphic on S x S.

Real conjugation of f and branch independence give g_(conj(z))=conj(g_z).
The Hermitian diagonal is a norm square. If it vanished, continuity would
make g_z(s)=0 for every s. On a large finite s interval the selected root
curve is nonconstant and accumulates inside S, forcing the nonzero f to
vanish identically. Thus G(conj(z),z)>0 throughout S, as required by Q3.

## Q3: quotient lemma used with the correct domain

Q3 matches the independently accepted conditional quotient lemma. Its
initial real-interval PSD yields a local common feature through Taylor
coefficient Gram matrices. The local nonzero Hermitian diagonal of D,
not global quotient holomorphy, supplies pathwise Cauchy bounds. These
continue the SAME Hilbert feature, with monodromy removed on simply
connected S. Only after obtaining global H is DH=N extended by the
identity theorem. Thus an uncancelled G zero is a legitimate contradiction
to the supposed R PSD; no analytic-kernel propagation across unremoved
quotient poles is assumed here.

## Q4: complete positive-tail ratios and both global majorants

The H(t) formula is exactly raw LV18, including the nonnegative full
n>=2 remainder and fixed positive lower bound. Substituting the definition
of f gives Q4 with exponent 9Delta/2 and no normalization change.
Its H ratio is bounded by (1+C_*)/h_- on the full real tail.

For Delta=v/lambda, exp(2Delta)-1>=2Delta gives the bound
exp[-v+9v/(2lambda)]<=exp(-v/2) when lambda>=9. For the radial ratio,

    Delta^2+2xDelta=2epsilon v=2xv/lambda.

Thus Delta<=v/lambda, and for x>=1/2,
exp(2Delta)-1>=2Delta+2Delta^2>=2Delta+Delta^2/x=2v/lambda.
The identical envelope follows. For each fixed v, lambda Delta->v and
lambda Delta^2->0. H tends to 1 at both arguments, so both full ratios
tend to exp(-v). No derivative of H or logarithmic concavity is needed
in this new localization argument.

## Q5: uniform zero transport with arbitrary multiplicity

Fix a nonreal source zero z0 strictly inside S. Since f is nonzero,
z0!=0 and its order m is finite; a_m!=0. All constants below may depend
on this fixed zero, m, and the compact w disk. No uniform-in-m assertion
is required or made.

For G, the exact substitution s=2epsilon v produces the normalization
2epsilon f(x)a_m epsilon^m. A local root branch around (z0,0), chosen
with root z0, exists because z0!=0; choose delta small enough to stay
in that local domain. For bounded v,w its expansion is

    z0+epsilon(w+v/z0)+O(epsilon^2).

The order-m factorization of f therefore gives the claimed pointwise
polynomial factor. On 0<=s<=delta the same factorization and bounded
local derivatives bound |f(root)| by C(epsilon R+s)^m. After division
by epsilon^m the integrand is dominated uniformly by
C exp(-v/2)(R+2v)^m, an integrable function. On bounded v intervals the
convergence is uniform in w. Truncating v first and then using this
uniform tail majorant proves local uniformity on compact w sets.

On s>=delta, Q2 bounds the entire second feature uniformly for z in a
fixed compact disk. Its normalized tail is at most

    C epsilon^(-m) exp[-delta/(4epsilon)],

up to a fixed constant factor, and tends to zero for any fixed m.
This explicitly pays the potentially dangerous small denominator.
Consequently Q6 is a full-integral locally uniform limit, not a formal
first-order source expansion.

For V, the exact substitution t=v/lambda gives precisely the three
factors in the candidate, including the complete linear weight and the
original endpoint. The denominator x+z0 is nonzero for large real x.
Since lambda epsilon=x, the second source displacement divided by epsilon
is w+v/x; it tends to w, which produces w^m rather than P_m.
On t<=delta the normalized source factor is bounded by C(R+v/x)^m,
and the weight by C(1+v). The same exponential envelope controls the
whole local integrand, uniformly in w. On t>=delta, the full LV2 bound
makes f(z+t) uniformly bounded and the tail is at most

    C epsilon^(-m) integral_(delta lambda)^infinity
          (1+v)exp(-v/2)dv.

Here epsilon=x/lambda. The exponential in lambda dominates every fixed
power epsilon^(-m)(1+lambda), so this tail tends to zero. Q7 follows
locally uniformly. These estimates handle every fixed finite multiplicity,
without assuming a simple zero, differentiating an asymptotic remainder,
or discarding any part of either original integral.

## Q6: Rouche gives a full unmatched pair zero

Expanding the integral polynomial gives the displayed coefficients because
integral_0^infinity exp(-v)v^k dv=k!. Its leading coefficient is one,
and P_m(0)=m!/z0^m is nonzero. A root exists and no root equals zero.
A sufficiently small closed disk around one root can therefore avoid
zero and have a zero-free boundary, regardless of root multiplicity.

Uniform Q6 convergence on that boundary supplies the strict Rouche
inequality for every sufficiently large finite x, giving at least one
zero of the FULL G slice inside. Uniform Q7 convergence on the entire
closed disk, where |w^m| has positive minimum, proves that the FULL V
slice has no zero there. The rescaled disk remains inside S for large x.
Thus Q8 is valid analytic existence of G(x,z_x)=0 and V(x,z_x)!=0.
No numerical location, effective threshold or source-zero simplicity is
being silently used.

Apply Q3 with D=G,N=V on S. Its global denominator diagonal condition
is Q2, and the real kernels are defined on every real interval. Any
all-finite PSD interval for R would force GH=V globally, contradicting
Q8. Hence R is not PSD on any nonempty real open interval. A negative
finite real coefficient row follows because R is real symmetric: a
negative complex quadratic form splits into real and imaginary parts.
Merging repeated nodes and the proved two-node positivity give the stated
lower bound of three distinct nodes, but no explicit rank or node list.

## Q7--Q8: exact obstruction scope

An identity V(x,y)=conj(eta(x))eta(y)G(x,y)M(x,y), with
arbitrary nonzero node factors and PSD M, would make V/G a diagonal
congruence of M on I. No regularity assumption on eta or M is needed.
This contradicts the established failure of R PSD and excludes precisely
that multiplicative/tensor repair of this radial Gram.

It does not exclude other features, nonlocal signal mixing, direct sums,
controlled signed decompositions, or positivity of V. In particular the
negative finite row belongs to R, not V; the Schur product implication
cannot be reversed. The arithmetic inputs are the accepted full theta
zero and full real tail, without a new assertion about prime factorization.

Final verdict: ACCEPT_RADIAL_GRAM_QUOTIENT_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.
No correction requested. Original V positivity and RH remain open.

lemma.review_text:
# Independent review: meromorphic positive-quotient continuation

Verdict: ACCEPT_CONDITIONAL_PSD_QUOTIENT_POLE_REMOVAL_LEMMA.
Candidate: RADIAL_QUOTIENT_LEMMA.md, SHA256
4c36857d42473687aaf7744f69a5de51a5ab5bd38bf6ad3a292f293902586a07.
Reviewer: /root/pairzero_geometry_review. Date: 2026-09-17.

The complete candidate was read. The proposed lemma is correct as stated.
No counterexample, missing sign assumption, or circular use of global
quotient holomorphy was found. Acceptance is conditional on its actual
all-finite PSD assumption and the global nonvanishing Hermitian diagonal
of D. It supplies neither assumption for a particular source quotient and
makes no statement that original V is PSD.

No search, new external theorem import, descendant, repository edit or
external dispatch was used. Only this assigned staging review is written.
The proof below is a direct independent audit of the displayed lemma;
the earlier feature-continuation reports are not needed as black boxes.

## 1. The initial common feature is justified

Choose a real interior point p of the PSD interval and a sufficiently
small conjugation-stable disk around it. Since D(p,p)>0, D has no zero
on the product of a smaller disk with itself. Q=N/D is holomorphic there.
A further interval shrink leaves a nonempty real interval with the given
all-family PSD property.

Applying finite differences of orders j,k at p to both variables of a
finite PSD kernel matrix and passing to the limit gives every finite
principal Taylor matrix

    B_jk=partial_1^j partial_2^k Q(p,p)/(j!k!)

positive semidefinite. This uses arbitrary complex coefficient vectors,
not merely positive real coefficients or finite checks of a fixed order.
One may construct the compatible vectors explicitly: give the formal
finitely supported sequence space the sesquilinear form with Gram matrix
B, quotient its null space, and complete. The coordinate classes are v_j
in one fixed Hilbert space.

On a smaller product disk where |Q|<=M, Cauchy's estimate gives
0<=B_jj<=M rho^(-2j), hence ||v_j||<=sqrt(M)rho^(-j).
The vector power series therefore converges absolutely and locally
uniformly in norm for |z-p|<rho. Its mixed inner-product expansion is
exactly Q(conj(z),w). Thus the initial feature exists without assuming
any global quotient regularity.

## 2. What the diagonal condition actually provides

For every z in S, D(conj(z),z)>0 implies D is nonzero in a product
neighborhood of (conj(z),z). Thus Q has a local holomorphic polarization
there and g(z)=Q(conj(z),z) is finite and real analytic throughout S.
Hermitian symmetry makes g real. Positivity of g at unvisited points is
not assumed or needed to start this step.

For a compact path gamma in S, its graph
{(conj(gamma(t)),gamma(t)):0<=t<=1} is compact in S x S. The continuous
|D| has a positive minimum on that graph. A sufficiently small uniform
product radius rho stays inside S x S and away from all D zeros in a
neighborhood of this graph. N and 1/D are bounded on the corresponding
closed neighborhood, giving one finite M. Neither this radius nor M is
asserted uniform over all of S or over pairs of distant path points.
That distinction is sufficient for the continuation argument.

## 3. Same-Hilbert continuation and the derivative estimate

Suppose a continued feature F is already defined near p. Its diagonal
identity ||F(z)||^2=g(z) determines its local polarization uniquely.
Equivalently, mixed derivatives of the real-analytic diagonal determine
all the coefficients of <F(z),F(w)>. Consequently

    <F^(j)(p)/j!,F^(k)(p)/k!>
      =partial_1^j partial_2^k Q(conj(p),p)/(j!k!).

In particular the diagonal coefficient is a squared norm. Cauchy's
estimate on the zero-free local product polydisk gives the bound in the
candidate, even when its radius is larger than the currently known F
neighborhood. Therefore

    sum_n F^(n)(p)(z-p)^n/n!

converges in THE SAME Hilbert space for |z-p|<rho. It agrees with F on
its old neighborhood by Taylor's theorem. The double inner-product series
converges absolutely and equals the local double Taylor series for Q on
the entire new product disk. In particular the extended F retains the
norm identity with g.

This argument only uses coefficients at a point where F already exists.
It does not presume PSD at a new point or use Q at a distant pair. If g
were negative somewhere, the construction would instead contradict the
initial PSD assumption upon reaching it; the proof does not need to
postulate nonnegative g globally.

Uniform continuity of a compact path and the common rho permit a finite
subdivision into steps shorter than, for example, rho/3. Repeating the
same construction extends the initial feature germ along the whole path.
All values and derivatives remain in the initial Hilbert space. No new
local Gram spaces or discretionary unitary transition maps are inserted.

## 4. Monodromy really is removed

The feature germ can be continued along EVERY path in S by the preceding
compact-path argument. Along an overlapping chain its continuation is
unique by equality of the old and new vector power series. On a simply
connected domain the usual subdivision-of-a-homotopy disk proof therefore
makes continuation path independent.

Alternatively apply each bounded linear functional on the fixed Hilbert
space to these continuations. Each resulting scalar holomorphic germ
continues along every path and has unique continuation on the simply
connected domain. It is single-valued. Bounded linear functionals separate
Hilbert vectors, so the vector germs continued along two paths agree.
Their local norm-convergent series then give one global holomorphic F.
This reasoning requires the stated simply connected S; that hypothesis is
not replaced merely by positivity on its real interval.

## 5. Off-diagonal poles are removed only at the final step

Define H(z,w)=<F(conj(z)),F(w)>. With the conjugate-linear first-slot
convention this is holomorphic in both UNBARRED variables. Joint
holomorphy follows directly from the local absolutely convergent double
vector-Taylor expansion and continuity of the Hilbert pairing.
Its polarization H(conj(z),w)=<F(z),F(w)> is Gram on all of S.

On the initial product disk H=Q. Hence D H-N is globally holomorphic on
S x S and vanishes on a nonempty OPEN product. Since S x S is connected,
the several-variable identity theorem gives D H=N everywhere (it can
also be applied one variable at a time). The identity involves no division
at a D zero. Thus it proves, rather than assumes, removability of every
possible off-diagonal quotient pole.

More precisely N is holomorphically divisible by D on all of S x S;
this includes the required multiplicities along its zero divisors, not
only coincidence of sets of zero points. D is not identically zero because
its Hermitian diagonal is positive. This is the exact consequence useful
for a proposed zero-mismatch contradiction.

## Final scope

The positive Hermitian diagonal of D is sufficient under the other stated
hypotheses. Its role is to supply zero-free local product neighborhoods
along every path, not a global zero-free product or positive numerator.
The construction never assumes the latter properties. No global logarithm
or fractional root occurs.

The full proof remains conditional on all-finite real-interval PSD of Q.
A separately proved denominator zero not cancelled by N would therefore
refute that quotient PSD entrance. It would not, without an additional
exact argument, refute positivity of N, of original V, or RH. Conversely
this lemma does not construct a sign proof for any source by itself.

Final verdict: ACCEPT_CONDITIONAL_PSD_QUOTIENT_POLE_REMOVAL_LEMMA.

accepted: Q2: even full theta source makes radial features holomorphic L2 maps on the full strip, with strictly positive Hermitian Gram diagonal
Q3: real-interval all-row PSD of a meromorphic quotient with nonzero denominator Hermitian diagonal forces global holomorphic Gram divisibility
Q4--Q5: exact full-source scaled integrals converge locally uniformly at every fixed multiplicity-m spatial zero, with complete tail bounds
Q6: radial Gram has an uncancelled complex pair zero; V/G is not PSD on any nonempty real open interval
Q7: no arbitrary nonzero node factors and PSD tensor multiplier can turn this exact radial Gram into V
parent_checks: square-root imaginary part bound including removable branch points
epsilon^-m tails vanish for both G and V without unproved derivative asymptotics
P_m(0)=m!/z0^m, so a root disk can avoid zero and V stays nonzero
only conditional global feature continuation, no prior holomorphy of V/G across Gram zeros
decision_effect: Exclude the all-rank positive Schur multiplier repair of the exact rank-two radial Gram. Entrywise comparison and two-node positivity remain valid. A different exact mechanism is required; this exclusion does not choose one.
